citations.quote:
Input a vector field $f(t,y)$, a finite grid $t_0,\ldots,t_N$, starting states $Y_0,Y_1\in\mathbb R^d$ (so $N\ge1$), and for each later step a prescribed closed ball $B_{n+1}\subset\mathbb R^d$ that specifies the admissible implicit branch. Before any evaluation, if either starting state has dimension different from $d$, return `invalid-input`; otherwise, if any time increment is nonpositive, return `invalid-grid`. Set $h_n=t_{n+1}-t_n$ and $r_n=h_n/h_{n-1}$ for $1\le n<N$.

For $n=1,\ldots,N-1$, form the equation

$$\frac{(1+2r_n)Z-(1+r_n)^2Y_n+r_n^2Y_{n-1}}{h_n(1+r_n)}=f(t_{n+1},Z).$$

If this equation has exactly one root $Z$ in $B_{n+1}$, set $Y_{n+1}=Z$ and continue. If it has no root there, return `no-root` with the computed prefix; if it has more than one root there, return `ambiguous-branch` with the computed prefix. If an evaluation of $f$ is undefined, return `evaluation-failure` with the prefix. On reaching $N$, return `completed` and $(Y_0,\ldots,Y_N)$. The procedure is defined for arbitrary positive adjacent step ratios; no convergence or accuracy property is part of this algorithm.

The coefficients are those obtained from the quadratic interpolation derivative in [[lem-variable-step-bdf2-interpolation-and-local-defect]]. A separate theorem gives the uniform ratio hypotheses needed for second-order convergence; they are not part of this algorithm.

Let $k\ge1$, $d\ge1$, and let $f:U\to\mathbb R^d$ be the right-hand side of a first-order initial-value problem on an open set $U\subseteq\mathbb R\times\mathbb R^d$, using the convention of [[def-first-order-ode-initial-value-problem-and-solution]]. A **constant-step $k$-step linear multistep method** has real coefficients $\alpha_0,\ldots,\alpha_k,\beta_0,\ldots,\beta_k$ with $\alpha_k\ne0$ and advances values by

$$\sum_{j=0}^k\alpha_jY_{n+j}=h\sum_{j=0}^k\beta_j f(t_{n+j},Y_{n+j}),\qquad t_{n+j}=t_n+jh,\quad h>0.$$

Multiplying all coefficients by the same nonzero scalar leaves the method unchanged; one may normalize $\alpha_k=1$. Its **characteristic polynomials** are

$$\rho(\zeta)=\sum_{j=0}^k\alpha_j\zeta^j,\qquad \sigma(\zeta)=\sum_{j=0}^k\beta_j\zeta^j.$$

For an exact solution $y$ with $p+1$ continuous derivatives, the **unscaled local residual** at $t_n$ is

$$\tau_n(h;y)=\sum_{j=0}^k\alpha_jy(t_n+jh)-h\sum_{j=0}^k\beta_jy'(t_n+jh).$$

The method has **order at least $p$**, where $p\ge1$ is an integer, if this residual is $O(h^{p+1})$ uniformly for admitted starting times in every fixed compact interval on which the indicated derivatives are bounded. It is **consistent** if it has order at least one. Equivalently, with the above coefficient convention, consistency is $\rho(1)=0$ and $\rho'(1)=\sigma(1)$.

The **root condition** is that every complex root of $\rho$ has modulus at most one and every root of modulus one has algebraic multiplicity one. The method is **zero-stable** if for each $T>0$ there is a constant $M_T$ independent of $N$ such that every solution of the homogeneous recurrence $\sum_j\alpha_jY_{n+j}=0$ on the uniform grid $h=T/N$ satisfies

$$\max_{0\le n\le N}\|Y_n\|_\infty\le M_T\max_{0\le j<k}\|Y_j\|_\infty.$$

Here $\|x\|_\infty=\max_{1\le i\le d}|x_i|$ for $x\in\mathbb R^d$. The root-condition equivalence for zero-stability is established separately.
